identity_evidence.quote: A 69-year-old man diagnosed with T-cell cutaneous lymphoma and ocular rosacea was referred to the Department of Ophthalmology of our tertiary center due to lesions in the ocular periphery of the right eye (OR).

attribution_limitations: The abstract says the patient presented with corneoscleral thinning five months after the treatment with mitomycin-C and interferon; the case text's "Five months later" opens a new paragraph after the oculoplastic referral and names no anchor. The abstract orders the MMC/interferon treatment before the return with thinning; the case-text interval is not tied to the referral, and the two five-month intervals are not equated.

The case text records worsening corneal edema, epithelial microcysts and reactive miosis at the four-month follow-up with BVCA maintained, while the discussion says the transplant led to an optical refractive result improving surface quality and the abstract says the approach established new tectonic support and corneal homeostasis. The author claims are kept review only.

The discussion says cutaneous T-cell lymphoma and rosacea were possibly leading to immunodeficiency, which with chemotherapy may have contributed to keratitis and corneal thinning. The case text does not name keratitis and names only "the infection"; hedged causes are not asserted.

The sentences after "In the first month after surgery" (adherence, BVCA, tonometry, pachymetry, B-ultrasound) and after "At the four-month follow-up" (worsening edema, microcysts, miosis, scleral thinning, eye closure, tonometry and BVCA maintained, declined triple procedure) do not each repeat a time. Times are attached only to the sentence that states them.

The first-month central corneal pachymetry is 670 µm in the case text, while Figure 3 (cited at the four-month follow-up) prints central and peripheral thickness numbers inside the image without units. Image-printed values are pixel content only and are not compared with the text value.
The "After one month" prescription of fluorometholone and MMC follows the interferon paragraph without naming the anchor; no order between the interferon start and the prescription is recorded.

After referral to the Oculoplastic Department the source says only that no surgery was required; it does not describe any oculoplastic examination or management, and ocular surface squamous neoplasia was never confirmed (impression cytology negative for dysplastic or neoplastic cells).

events.description: Tectonic corneoscleral lamellar anterior transplant with donor cornea and sclera

evidence.quote: A partial transplant was performed using a donor cornea, which was placed upside down in the artificial chamber with the endothelium facing upwards (Figure 2).
This was achieved using a micrometer diamond knife entering at a depth of 100 µm as peripherally as possible.
The sclera was then detached from the cornea through the limbus using scissors, leaving a sclera pedicle with a base of 4 mm and a width of 2 mm.
The receiving cornea was prepared by manually removing the epithelium with a type-15 scalpel.

The donor cornea was positioned over the recipient’s cornea and sutured through the limbus with superficial corneal sutures to the donor cornea and deep in the recipient’s limbus to allow perfect positioning and epithelial migration.
The donor sclera was similarly sutured over the thinned recipient sclera and covered with the patient’s inferior conjunctival epithelium.
